content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text uses a verse's not naming whose body is the channel as the reason to leave the point open, which is the kind of ground the rule governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"The phrase 'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary' weighed as forbidding any use of a verse's silence to support UNDERDETERMINED, versus forbidding only UNDERDETERMINED based on one verse in isolation when other verses are in view.","why":"The judge makes the lack of a named channel in Acts 2:30 the ground for UNDERDETERMINED, so it breaches K-S2."}
